cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has a message, and it opens with the one word you NEVER want at the top of a letter: woe. It's for Ariel, the city where David, Israel's king, camped. Isaiah tells them to let their festivals keep coming around, year upon year.

cards.question: The LORD says He will constrain Ariel. Then there will be ___ and lamentation.

cards.text: Then the LORD says Ariel "will be like an altar hearth before Me." Friend, I've worked next to ovens my whole life, and even I felt the heat coming off that line.

cards.question: David once camped at Ariel. Now the LORD says someone will camp in a circle around the city. Who?

cards.text: Towers. Siege works. A full circle around the city. When I say ringed in, friend, I mean RINGED in.

cards.question: Ariel will be brought low. Where does Isaiah say her muffled words will come from?

cards.text: Her voice will be like a spirit from the ground, a whisper out of the dust. Baker, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer. A muffled whisper out of the dust? That was my whole personality.
But then the picture flips. Ariel was the one in the dust a minute ago. Now her many foes will be like fine dust, and the ruthless crowd like blowing chaff.

cards.question: Isaiah compares Ariel's many foes to fine dust and blowing chaff. What does that picture say about them?

answers.text: They will settle in for good

cards.question: True or false: Right after the dust and chaff picture, Isaiah says what comes next arrives slowly, over many years.

cards.text: Suddenly, in an instant, the LORD of Hosts visits with thunder and earthquake and loud noise, with windstorm and tempest and consuming flame of fire. That's EVERY weather alert on your phone going off at the same time.
And all the many nations that go out to battle against Ariel, laying siege and attacking her? They will be like a dream, like a vision in the night.

cards.question: Isaiah compares the attacking nations to a hungry man who dreams he is eating. What happens when he wakes up?
True or false: Isaiah also pictures a thirsty man who dreams he is drinking and wakes up satisfied.
Just like the hungry dreamer, the many nations who go to battle against Mount Zion come away ___.

cards.text: Now Isaiah's words get sharp: stop and be astonished, blind yourselves and be sightless. Then he says be drunk and stagger, but there's a catch in how he says it.

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says this staggering comes from strong drink.
Isaiah says the LORD has poured something out. What is it?
Along with that deep sleep, the LORD shuts some people's eyes and covers their heads. Who are they?

cards.text: And the entire vision will be to them like words sealed in a scroll. It's like getting handed a locked phone when nobody in the room knows the passcode.

cards.question: True or false: If the sealed scroll is handed to someone who can read, he will say he can't read it because it is sealed.
Or if the scroll is handed to someone unable to read, his answer is that he ___ read.

cards.text: Then the Lord speaks about these people, and He looks at two things: their mouths and their hearts.

cards.question: These people draw near to the Lord with their mouths and honor Him with their lips. But their hearts are ___ Him.

cards.text: Mouth in the room, heart somewhere else. It's like singing happy birthday on a video call with your camera off, answering emails the whole time.

cards.question: With their hearts far away, what does the Lord say their worship of Him is?

cards.text: So the Lord says He will again confound these people. Friend, I've been confounded by an oven timer before, so I am LEANING in to hear how.

cards.question: How does the Lord say He will confound these people?
True or false: The Lord says the wisdom of the wise will grow.

cards.text: The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden. If the smartest folks in the room come up empty, a stamper who lived in a junk drawer is gonna sit down and LISTEN.

findings.problem: The card is four sentences: 'Towers.' 'Siege works.' 'A full circle around the city.' and the joke line. Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke 'When I say ringed in, friend, I mean RINGED in' only repeats a phrase. Papa Dorin never said 'ringed in' earlier, so the line has nothing to call back to and doesn't land as a real laugh.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card is four sentences, one retelling verse 4 and three for the junk drawer joke. Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card is three sentences: 'But then the picture flips.' plus 'Ariel was the one in the dust a minute ago.' plus 'Now her many foes...'. Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The statement says 'what comes next arrives slowly' without naming what comes next, so the baker doesn't know what is being timed. No earlier card hints at the timing either, which leaves the baker with a coin flip.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Isaiah says this staggering comes from strong drink' points back to the staggering on story card 1, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say what the staggering is or who is told to stagger.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question already says the person is 'unable to read', which gives away 'cannot' and rules out 'will' and 'might'. The blank tests nothing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
